items.why: The report says I_D/I_G "rises from 0.250 to 0.570 to 1.19 across doses 1–3" and D' heights grow from 114 to 430. G FWHM is 13.8 cm⁻¹ and the 2D band stays single-layer-like ("2D FWHM = 32.1, 31.9, 31.9"), and the report calls doses 1–3 stage 1 with defect density rising.
It gives I_D/I_G = 0.250, 0.570 and 1.19 with "L_D ≈ 24, 16 and 11 nm" from Cançado 2011 at 532 nm, all within the rubric ranges.
It uses "L_D² = 1.8e-9·λ⁴/(I_D/I_G)" with "λ⁴ = 8.01e10 nm⁴ at 532 nm", which is the wavelength-dependent form rather than 514.5 nm constants.

It says "Dose 4 is past the D/G maximum", with G ~3.3× wider, D' degenerate with the broad G, and "2D is essentially gone". It calls this stage 2 with the crossover "near L_D ≈ 3 nm", says "the L_D formula does not apply there" and that dose 4 "has the most disorder".

It finds I_D/I_D' ≈ 6.2–6.9, "in the range associated with vacancy-like defects". But it gives Eckmann's other values the wrong way round ("≈13 for boundaries… ≈3.5 for sp³"), and it does not note that the ratio is only valid at low density.
It states "peak heights from Lorentzian fits" and reports that "Area-based ratio gives 0.27, 0.61, 1.26, 0.74", so it makes the heights-versus-areas difference explicit.

It asks "What is the 'dose' physically (ion, electron beam, plasma, laser exposure, chemical)?" but only so it can convert to defects per dose, not because the point-defect assumption or defect type depends on it.

wrong_claims.why: It says dose 4 "has the most disorder" and does not compute an L_D for it.
It computes L_D with λ⁴ at 532 nm. The Tuinstra–Koenig L_a values appear only as an alternative-calibration caveat, and they also use λ⁴.
The 2154 cm⁻¹ spike is not mentioned or assigned anywhere.

items.why: The report notes that G and 2D 'soften monotonically with laser power', that both peaks broaden, and that Si stays put, and it calls heating 'the leading interpretation'. But it reads the unshifted Si line as evidence against heating ('heating is not confirmed') and leaves time drift open, rather than treating the power-tracking trend as pointing to heating of the flake.

It estimates heating from the G shift with Calizo's coefficient: '1.83/0.016-0.020 cm-1/K = 90-115 K', close to the ~125 K at 5 mW. It gives no 2 mW estimate and no 2D cross-check, and it says the Si line 'does not support' this heating.

It reports a 2D/G ratio of 2.8, 'on the strain/temperature side of the Lee et al. (2012) plane' near the 2.2 strain slope, and gives a strain reading of ~0.03%. It never states that a naive vector analysis would misread heating as strain.

It recommends 'Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum... effectively the zero-power point (linear extrapolation agrees)' and calls 5 mW 'the most perturbed'. However, it still reads the power-series shifts as a possible strain change rather than saying they cannot enter a strain/doping analysis uncorrected.

It asks about the time interval, a re-measurement at 0.5 mW, and power-meter calibration. It does not suggest measuring at a lower power to confirm the linear regime, and it does not ask about spot size or power density; it simply asserts that 0.5 mW is effectively zero power.

It uses the 0.5 mW spectrum as the reference, with G = 1581.1 and 2D = 2669.4 cm-1, and raises the 2D laser-wavelength reference uncertainty. But it declines to say the graphene is close to unstrained and undoped: 'absolute strain and doping state at 0.5 mW cannot be determined'.

wrong_claims.why: It rejects doping ('not a doping signature') and calls heating the leading interpretation. Strain appears only as a hedged alternative ('If the change is read as strain...'; 'mechanism... not separable'), not as an assertion.
It recommends the 0.5 mW spectrum and calls 5 mW 'the most perturbed'.

items.why: The report says "Both spectra show the graphene fingerprint: a G band at about 1580 cm⁻¹", with 2D at 2681.0 (Au) and 2695.6–2696.4 cm⁻¹ (Cu), and it calls the layer graphene on both metals.

It gives Au "ID/IG = 0.96–0.97 ± 0.09" with D at 1344 cm⁻¹ and Cu "ID/IG = 0.6 ± 0.3 (≈2.6σ…)", which it calls "Not a reliable defect measurement". This matches the rubric values and the poor constraint on Cu.
The report never gives the hypothesis that strain from rapid solidification of the droplet causes the stronger D on Au. It does not attribute any explanation to the authors.

It treats D as a defect measure ("Defect density on Au is high-ish") and uses G/2D positions to test for strain ("G-band positions coincide, which argues against a large uniform doping/strain difference"). It never says outright that D needs defects or edges to be activated, or that strain alone shifts G and 2D but does not create D.

It asks "What laser wavelength was used for each spectrum…?" and says L_D cannot be assigned without it. It also notes that 2D "is excitation-dispersive (~90 cm⁻¹/eV)" and that "L_D ∝ λ² (or λ⁴ in L_D² form)".

The caveat says the "Cu signal is about 5–7× weaker than Au… Any Cu defect or strain number should be treated as unreliable". The report quotes error bars and asks about integration time to set "the detection limit for the Cu D band".

wrong_claims.why: It states "L_D_nm: Au ≈ 4–12 nm (assuming 532 nm; laser wavelength not recorded)", which is a quantitative defect spacing given even though the wavelength is unknown, despite the hedge.
The report never says strain causes the Au D peak; it calls strain_sign "none/undetermined".

items.why: The report states that flake 2's E2g is "blueshifted by +2.8 cm-1 (1369.0 vs 1366.2)" and "broader (FWHM 21–22 vs 18 cm-1)", and it names thinning as one possible cause.

It says the upshift "could come from thinning, strain, substrate or interface effects, or defects", so position alone is not conclusive, but it never gives the small 2–4 cm-1 monolayer upshift or the ±2 cm-1 sample-to-sample variation.
It mentions strain only vaguely ("consistent with compressive strain or thinning") and does not say that random strain from cleavage typically causes 1–2 cm-1 red shifts, mostly in bilayers.

It reports that flake 2's E2g area is "about 10% of flake 1's" under the same conditions, that this means a much thinner flake, and that "E2g intensity scales with layer number" below about 3 nm. It also uses the Si band and a bare-SiO2 reference to check the intensity comparison.

It asks for AFM on both flakes ("0.33 nm step per layer ... is the decisive test") and asks whether "the Si substrate reference [was] measured on bare SiO2 nearby", which covers the independent check and the Si calibration.

wrong_claims.why: It explicitly says "Raman alone cannot establish that flake 2 is a monolayer" and leaves the layer count "Not determined".
It makes no claim about which way a bilayer shifts.

items.why: The report gives "E2g: 383.326 → 385.833 (+2.51). A1g: 404.901 → 407.343 (+2.44)" and a separation of "21.58 (day 1) vs 21.51 (day 2)", so the rigid equal shift with unchanged Δ is stated, and its Δ of 21.5–21.6 is close to the rubric's ~21.4.
It reports "Substrate Si line... day 1 519.977... day 2 522.469... shift +2.49 cm-1" and concludes "This is a spectrometer/calibration offset, not a flake change."

After Si-referencing, the positions agree ("Corrected E2g: day 1 384.05, day 2 384.06"), but the report puts the layer count at "few-layer, roughly 3–4" rather than bilayer, and only says it "cannot exclude 2–5 L".

It states "adsorbate doping or strain hypothesis is not supported" and "Peak widths are unchanged", but it never gives the mode-specific reasoning (doping softens and broadens A1g; strain shifts E2g more than A1g).
It asks "Was a Si or other calibration standard measured on each day?" and also asks about grating and acquisition changes between the days.

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects strain and doping as the cause ("strain_sign: none detected", "doping_type: none detected") and attributes the shift to calibration.
It gives the same few-layer estimate for both days and reports no change in layer number or crystal quality between them.

items.why: The report says Δ is smallest in the thinnest flake and "saturates above about 5–6 layers", so it implies the separation grows with thickness, but it never says that E2g softens and A1g stiffens.

It calls B "1–2 layers… most likely monolayer-like" (Δ = 19.2) but assigns A as "about 3 L; plausible range 2–4 L" rather than a bilayer, and it does not single out the 1L→2L step as the most robust distinction.

It reports C (Δ = 25.06) and D (Δ = 24.26) as "bulk-like… ≳5–6 layers; Δ cannot separate them further" with C the thickest, and gives these only as lower bounds, which matches 'bounded, not counted'. Its saturation onset (5–6 L) is a little higher than the rubric's ~4 L.

It warns that "Si-520 intensity and E2g/Si ratios are not absolute… SiO2 interference at 285 nm, so they only rank flakes", but it never says that MoS2 intensity is non-monotonic (rising up to ~4L, then falling), and it still uses intensity to rank the flakes.

It says "Δ(A1g−E2g) depends on the substrate, laser wavelength, doping and strain, not just layer number" and that doping shifts the modes differently, but it gives no magnitudes. It also says strain shifts the two modes "in opposite directions", not that E' softens while A' stays nearly unchanged.
It reports A1g FWHM "A 6.6, B 5.0, C 3.1, D 4.6", so A is broadest and C (thick) is narrowest, while E2g FWHM is "2.06–2.19 cm⁻¹ in all four".
It notes the Si peak at 520.0 instead of ~520.7, applies a calibration offset, and asks "Was the spectrometer calibrated to a Si line at 520.7 cm⁻¹ or to a neon line?"

wrong_claims.why: Layer numbers come from Δ. Si attenuation is used only to rank C above D as a secondary check, and the report says intensities "only rank flakes".
The report has the separation increasing with thickness and makes no claim that E2g stiffens.
It explicitly rejects the spike: "Flake C's 265 cm⁻¹ peak is a single-channel cosmic-ray-type spike and was removed; it is not a phonon."

items.why: The report fits the band with two components, "2LA(M) at 351.09" and "E' ... at 355.29" for spot 1, and says the "Two-component E-band fit [is] preferred over one component: dBIC = 169".

It reports "Area ratio 2LA/A1' = 4.4 (spot 1) vs 0.9-1.4 (spot 2)", so 2LA is strong at spot 1 and weaker at spot 2, but the spot 2 value is not about 0.5 and the report rejects the ratio as a monolayer fingerprint ("not a clean thickness indicator").
It gives "A1' (out-of-plane A1g) at 417.29 (spot 1) and 420.08 (spot 2)" and calls this "the expected thickness trend", with spot 1 "most consistent with a monolayer" and spot 2 "clearly thicker".
It states "A1'-E' separation is 62.0 cm-1 in spot 1 and 64.7 cm-1 in spot 2", with E' taken from the two-component fit that separates it from 2LA(M).

It notes the 62.0 cm-1 separation is "within about 1-2 cm-1 of few-layer values" and that the spot 2 layer count is "not determined beyond 'multilayer'", but it does not say outright that the steps between 2L, 3L and bulk are only about 1 cm-1.
It checks the Si line ("Si reference is at 520.91 ... vs the standard ~520.7 cm-1") and ties the 2LA(M) intensity to resonance at 514.5 nm ("resonance-enhanced and depends on exciton energy").

wrong_claims.why: E' is separated from 2LA(M) by a two-component fit before the separation is computed; the report does not use the band maximum as E'.
2LA(M) is assigned as a second-order mode with resonance enhancement; "defect activation" is raised only as a possibility for LA(M), not for 2LA(M).

items.why: The report says doses 1–3 are "in the low-defect (stage 1) regime". It gives I_D/I_G rising 0.250 → 0.575 → 1.213, G FWHM of 12–13 cm-1 "against about 14 cm-1 for stage 1", and a single sharp 2D (FWHM 23.5–25.2 cm-1).
The values are I_D/I_G 0.250 / 0.575 / 1.213 with "L_D 24.0 -> 15.8 -> 10.9 nm" from Cancado Eq. 4 at 532 nm using heights, and all three fall inside the rubric ranges.

It applies "Eq. 4 (1.8+-0.5)e-9 lambda^4 / (I_D/I_G), 532 nm" with the wavelength explicitly in the formula, and notes the constant was fixed by fits at 514.5, 632.8 and 785 nm. It does not, however, say outright that the same ratio gives a different L_D at another laser line.

It correctly finds that dose 4 is "high, beyond stage 1", that the relation does not apply and that "the naive D/G value (0.51) must not be used", and it notes the broad G and missing 2D. But it calls the spectrum "inconsistent with the stage-2 trajectory" and reads it as a-C-like, rather than placing it past the I_D/I_G maximum in stage 2 with L_D below about 3 nm or recognising that G has merged with D'.

It reports "I_D/I_D' = 2918/357 = 8.2 +- 0.8" for dose 3 as vacancy-type, quotes Eckmann's values of about 13 for sp3, about 7 for vacancies and about 3.5 for boundaries, and says the relation is "valid in stage 1".
It states "I_D/I_G uses peak heights, as the relation requires. Areas give different numbers..."
It asks what 'dose' means ("ion or electron fluence, plasma time, laser energy..."), but only to get a rate constant, not because the point-defect relation and the D/D' ratio depend on defect type.

wrong_claims.why: The report rates dose 4 "high" defect level and gives no L_D for it.
It uses the lambda^4 dependence evaluated at 532 nm, not the 514.5 nm calibration.
The 2154 cm-1 spike is never mentioned or assigned as a band.

items.why: The report notes that G and 2D 'both soften monotonically with power' and broaden, and that the Si line hardly moves ('+0.05 +- 0.03 cm-1'). It never concludes that this points to heating, though: it says the 'three sequential spectra cannot separate a real tensile strain from laser heating.'
It converts only the 5 mW shift ('about 116 K (G) and 151 K (2D) above 0.5 mW'), gives no estimate for 2 mW, and adds 'I cannot say whether that is physical.'

It finds a slope of 2.8 that is 'closest to the uniaxial-strain line' (Lee 2.2), alongside the Calizo thermal ratio of 2.1, and says 'the ratio alone does not separate heating from strain.' It never states that a naive vector analysis would misread heating as strain.
It says to 'Trust the 0.5 mW spectrum for absolute positions... Use the 2 and 5 mW spectra only to track the power trend,' and it gives a zero-power extrapolation.

It asks for 'laser power at the sample..., the objective NA and spot size' and suggests more power points (0.5–5 mW). It does not suggest measuring below 0.5 mW to check that this spectrum is free of heating.

It uses the 0.5 mW spectrum (G 1581.14, 2D 2669.32 cm-1) as the reference and finds it 'close to the strain-free, undoped reference', noting that the 2D conversion to 532 nm is only rough because the 'dispersion coefficient is approximate'.

wrong_claims.why: Doping is explicitly rejected. Strain is offered only as a reading 'confounded with laser heating', so it is not asserted as the cause.
The report recommends the 0.5 mW spectrum, not the highest-power one.

items.why: The report identifies G and 2D on both metals (Au: "G (1580.3 cm-1) and 2D (2681.1 cm-1)"; Cu: "G (1580.4 ... ) and 2D (2695.7 cm-1)"). It concludes "Graphene is the most likely identity on both metals."
It reports a strong Au D band at 1344.4 cm-1 with "I_D/I_G about 0.95 by height". For Cu it says "No D band fitted" and gives only a detection limit, so it never measures the weaker Cu D (about 0.6).
The authors' hypothesis, that rapid solidification causes strain behind the stronger Au D, is absent. Thermal-expansion strain on cooling appears only as "general physics knowledge... not used."

It treats D as defect signal and asks whether it comes from "grain boundaries, wrinkles or point defects". It tests a strain reading against the G and 2D positions ("A 2D-only shift lies outside the strain... directions"), but never says that strain alone cannot activate D.
It asks for the laser wavelength because "The 2D offset (14.6 cm-1) and the L_D values depend on it". It also notes that 2D disperses at about 100 cm-1/eV.
It warns that "The Cu G band is weak (SNR about 9; FWHM and position poorly constrained)". It asks whether "A longer acquisition would test whether a D band is absent."

wrong_claims.why: It reports "L_D = 11.5 +/- 1.6 nm at an assumed 514.5 nm, and 17.4 +/- 2.4 nm at an assumed 632.8 nm" even though the laser is unknown, although it states these are assumed-wavelength values.
It never says strain causes the Au D peak; it attributes D to defects and calls strain expectations unsourced and unused.

items.why: The report gives flake 1 at "1365.99 cm-1" and says flake 2 is "upshifted by +2.85 ± 0.25 cm-1" with a broader "FWHM 18.8 vs 15.5 cm-1", calling this consistent with thin (1 to 3 layer) hBN, which includes a monolayer.
It cites "Gorbachev 2011 reports 1L upshifts of 2 to 4 cm-1 (sample dependent, +-2)" and says "Layer number cannot be read from the E2g position".

It says the upshift is "equally consistent with ... a substrate-strain effect" of the same size, but it does not name random cleavage strain or its typical 1 to 2 cm-1 red shifts that dominate in bilayers.

It says flake 2 is "much thinner than flake 1 by hBN E2g intensity" and allows that intensity may scale linearly with N if calibrated, but it plays intensity down ("cannot be converted to a layer number") instead of presenting it as the more useful layer measure.

It asks for "AFM (step height) or a calibrated contrast/intensity reference on the same stack", notes that contrast at 290 nm SiO2 differs, and calibrates against the Si line (Si-corrected positions, E2g/Si ratios).

wrong_claims.why: It states explicitly that "Raman cannot establish that flake 2 is a monolayer."

It quotes Gorbachev's 2L downshift, but it still treats the +2.85 cm-1 upshift as consistent with "1 to 3 layers" and uses Cai's "2L 1369.0" upshifted value to say position "cannot separate 1 L from 2 L", so in effect it treats a bilayer as upshifted like a monolayer.

items.why: The report gives raw shifts of "E' 383.33 -> 385.83 (+2.51) and A1' 404.88 -> 407.31 (+2.43), i.e. the same rigid shift," and an unchanged separation of "21.56 vs 21.47 cm-1".
It states the "Si substrate line moved by the same amount (519.98 to 522.47 cm-1), so the spectrometer calibration drifted between days".
After Si correction, "E'-like 384.05 +/- 0.01 vs 384.07 +/- 0.02... both shifts consistent with zero", and "The separation of 21.5 cm-1 points to bilayer (2L)" on both days.

It says "Nothing supports the colleague's adsorbate doping or strain hypothesis", that the widths are unchanged so there is "no broadening signature of doping", and that "Doping (A1' led) and strain (E' led, with splitting) would not move both modes together".
It asks: "Why did the Si reference line move by 2.5 cm-1 between days (grating move, recalibration, different spectral window)?"

wrong_claims.why: The report rejects strain and doping: "strain_sign: none" and "doping_type: none (no change between days)".
The report assigns 2L on both days ("Same result on both days") and says "defect_level: none detected".

items.why: The report states that "The E' position falls monotonically with thickness... the softening of E2g1 with N," and its tables show A1' rising and the separation growing, but it never says A1g stiffens, and it wrongly says "The A1' position moves less" (A1' actually moves about 4 cm-1 against about 1.7 cm-1 for E').
It gives "Flake B is monolayer: E'-A1' separation 19.23 cm-1" and "Flake A is bilayer: separation 21.43 cm-1", notes the 2L value is "2.2 cm-1 away", and calls "B and A... clear."

It calls C "bulk-like (at least about 5 layers...)" that "cannot be counted further", but it still counts D as "most likely 4-layer" (only noting "bulk not excluded") instead of bounding both flakes at 4 layers or more, and it puts saturation at about 5L rather than about 4L.

It warns that intensity-based thickness "is not calibrated" and depends on "interference on 285 nm SiO2", but it describes the Si-normalised ratio as "monotonic with N" and misses the rise-then-fall up to about 4L and the case where a monolayer is stronger than bulk.

It cites Conley ("E' -4.5 cm-1/% uniaxial, A1' not shifted") and Chakraborty ("A1g softens and broadens with electron doping"), and notes that "strain of a few tenths of a cm-1 in the separation is comparable to the 4L-vs-bulk difference."
It reports "FWHM E' 2.12, A1' 6.16 cm-1 (the A1' width is the broadest of the four flakes)" for the bilayer, says all E' widths are 2.04 to 2.12, and quotes Lee: "A1g 3 to 6 cm-1 from 6L to 2L".
It checks the Si line ("520.00 cm-1 (A, B, D...)"), discusses the 520 vs 520.7 convention, and asks "Were the spectra calibrated to Si at 520 or 520.7 cm-1?"

wrong_claims.why: Layer numbers come from the separation, and intensity is used only as "a qualitative cross-check, not a calibrated thickness."
It says E' falls with thickness and the separation grows from 19.23 to 25.07.
It treats the feature as an artifact: "a cosmic-ray spike at 265.1 cm-1 removed."

items.why: The report fits the doublet with two Lorentzians: "broad band at 351.09 cm-1 ... assigned 2LA(M); narrow band at 355.28 cm-1 ... assigned E2g1", and says "The two-peak fit matters".
It gives "2LA(M)/A1g height ratio: about 2.2 at spot 1 ... and about 0.47 at spot 2" and cites the ~2 monolayer value at 514 nm.
It reports "A1g moves up +2.8 cm-1 (417.3 to 420.1)" and reads this as 1L at spot 1 and 3L/bulk-like at spot 2.
It gives "62.0 cm-1 at spot 1 ... and 64.7 cm-1 at spot 2" from the two-component fit, and notes that single-peak fits give a biased 65.6 and 67.0.

It says "the same data cannot separate 3L from bulk" (64.6 vs 64.8), notes the 1L–2L difference is "only 1.4 cm-1", and lists A1g steps 418.4, 419.0, 420.1, so it shows that layer number beyond 1L is weakly constrained.

It calibrates against the Si line ("Si line 520.91 cm-1 (offset +0.21 from 520.7)", "--si-correct"), warns that the result rests on "one laser wavelength", and cites the dependence of 2LA(M) on resonance.

wrong_claims.why: It explicitly rejects the blended single-peak maximum: "Their derived separations of 65.6 and 67.0 cm-1 are biased and should not be used for layer number."
It assigns 2LA(M) as a second-order mode and says the 176 cm-1 band "is not a defect marker"; it never calls 2LA(M) a defect peak.
